title: Timing of Restitution on a Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
How much of a sum over-recovered is put back on a Keyturn Host Payout Account at once turns on how far the claims made under the host's Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment have got, because the rest follows only when the claim that produced the recovery is settled.

**Where money has been paid out on a claim under the enrolment**, the whole of the sum over-recovered is put back, that is 100 percent of it.

**Where no money has been paid out on a claim under the enrolment and a claim has been appraised under it in the twelve months up to that day**, half of the sum over-recovered is put back now, that is 50 percent of it.

**In every other case**, a fifth of it is put back now, that is 20 percent of it.

The share is taken on the sum over-recovered and the result is rounded half to even to two decimal places.

## Points of judgement

**Both conditions of the second case must hold.** A claim appraised under the enrolment within the twelve months up to that day puts the account in the second case only while no money has been paid out on a claim under that enrolment; once a payment has been made, the first case governs whatever the appraisals show.

**Where nothing has been appraised in that period and nothing has been paid out**, neither of the first two cases is met and the third governs.

**On hypothetical figures.** Where the sum over-recovered is 200.00 USD: 200.00 USD is put back where money has been paid out on a claim under the enrolment; 100.00 USD where nothing has been paid out but a claim has been appraised under it in the twelve months up to that day; and 40.00 USD in every other case.

The records that settle it are the claim records held under the host's Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment, which show the payments made on claims under that enrolment and the day each appraisal was made.
